messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Bilateral symmetry wrt groups
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Dean Adams,

Thank you for explaining this. I look forward to improvements in Geomorph package.

---

Regards

Rochishnu Dutta

From: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com <geomorph-...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of Adams, Dean [EEOB]
Sent: 30 September 2019 21:22
To: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com
Subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Bilateral symmetry wrt groups

RD,

Presently, geomorph does not allow for additional factors in the bilat.symmetry model. In theory this can be done with more general code; and in fact it is on the list of possible upgrades for a future version of geomorph. But we presently don’t only allow for a single additional factor, as in our view that is limiting (why not 2 factors? Interactions, etc.?). We prefer implementing fully flexible statistical approaches, but devising this for the case of symmetry is not trivial. This is why the additional factor (as in MorphoJ) is not currently in bilat.symmetry.

Thus at present you have two options. First, one could run the bilat.symmetry as you have done, extract the FA component and then run a comparison of groups on the FA component. Here you are able to compare levels of FA among groups, but not in the context of the full symmetry analysis. This may be less desirable because in this case the variation among groups is not evaluated relative to the rest of the model (whether or not that is an issue is something one could discuss).

The second option is more involved. Basically, one can run a linear model on the data using procD.lm, and include the requisite components for DA and FA.  However, doing so will require replicating some of the underlying code in bilat.symmetry to up-front extract the DA and FA components properly.  Not easy if one is an R-novice, but it is possible to do.

Dean

Dr. Dean C. Adams

Director of Graduate Education, EEB Program

Professor

Department of Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology

Iowa State University

https://www.eeob.iastate.edu/faculty/adams/

phone: 515-294-3834

From: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com <geomorph-...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of Rochishnu Dutta
Sent: Monday, September 30, 2019 4:21 AM
To: geomorph R package <geomorph-...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: [geomorph-r-package] Bilateral symmetry wrt groups

Hi all,

I have been trying to assess fluctuating asymmetry in Drosophila wings. I have used the following code:

WingDros_gdf = geomorph.data.frame(wingshape = WingDros_tps,ind = WingDros_var$IDs,

                                   regime = WingDros_var$Sel.Reg, block = as.factor(WingDros_var$Block),

                                   side = as.integer(WingDros_var$Side),

                                   replicate = as.factor(WingDros_var$User.Replicate),

                                   group = WingDros_var$Group)

WingDros_sym = bilat.symmetry(A=wingshape, ind=ind, side=side, object.sym=FALSE,

                              RRPP=TRUE, replicate = replicate, iter = 999, seed = 47,

                              data=WingDros_gdf)

I get shape anova results which are perfectly fine. However, I would like to check differences in fluctuating asymmetry among various groups and get a result such as in the attached picture. I realise that this is possible to do in MorphoJ that Dr. Klingenberg uses. But I would like to replicate this study in Geomorph. Since I am new to geomorph, I am unable to incorporate groups in shape anova using above Geomorph syntaxes.

Any help or indication as to how to go about this will be really helpful.

Regards

RD

messages.subject: digitsurface mean centers regardless of setting
messages.subject_clean: digitsurface mean centers regardless of setting
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Quick background - we have four laryngeal cartilages which were micro-ct scanned in anatomical position. The cartilage were then saved as four separate surface files and landmarks / semilandmarks were acquired using various Geomorph functions, including digitsurface.

Although we set the center=FALSE option, the surface always ends up centered at the origin after using digitsurface.

We are hoping to keep the surfaces in their original global coordinate system so that the four cartilages can then be treated as a single structure for superimposition purposes.

We would appreciate assistance in this.

Here is the code (M20Al and P12Al are ply files):

lm<-digit.fixed(M20Al,12,center=FALSE)

buildtemplate(M20Al,lm,50,center=FALSE)

LMdata<-digitsurface(P12Al,12, ptsize=1,center=FALSE)

Thanks in advance!

-Karen

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Shell reconstruccions in fossils
messages.body_plain:
This question is a bit outside of the geomorph realm, as it is data pre-processing.

Not quite sure what you mean by ‘reconstruction’. If this means 3D imaging, then one requires a scanning devise. If this means ‘fixing’ broken components, then I suggest you investigate the text ‘Virtual Anthropology’. They discuss methods of reconstruction of imperfect specimens prior to landmark data collection.

Dean

messages.subject: Different symmetric component from bilat.symmetry (geomorph) and procSym (Morpho)
messages.subject_clean: Different symmetric component from bilat.symmetry (geomorph) and procSym (Morpho)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I want to extract symmetric component from GPA of an object with object symmetry. I tried both bilat.symmetr in geomorph and procSym in Morpho. I get some confusing results.

library(Morpho)
library(geomorph)

data(boneData)
left <- c(4,6,8)
right <- c(3,5,7)
pairedLM <- cbind(left,right)

gpa <- bilat.symmetry(boneLM, object.sym = T, land.pairs = pairedLM, ind = 1:dim(boneLM)[3])
gpa$symm.shape[,,1]

             [,1]          [,2]         [,3]
 [1,]  0.34732242  2.407271e-17 -0.016892962
 [2,]  0.39146334  4.599880e-17 -0.005335477
 [3,]  0.35596324 -4.638598e-02  0.033862782
 [4,]  0.35596324  4.638598e-02  0.033862782
 [5,] -0.27746925 -7.299494e-02  0.018315568
 [6,] -0.27746925  7.299494e-02  0.018315568
 [7,] -0.24952878 -1.218970e-01  0.037420485
 [8,] -0.24952878  1.218970e-01  0.037420485
 [9,] -0.35308247 -6.961152e-17 -0.018107224
[10,] -0.04363372 -1.809286e-16 -0.138862006

As expected, gpa$symm.shape[3,,1] and gpa$symm.shape[4,,1] differ in sign of just one of the x, y, and z values. The same holds for gpa$symm.shape[5,,1] and gpa$symm.shape[6,,1] and gpa$symm.shape[7,,1] and gpa$symm.shape[8,,1]. However, I tried Morpho as follows:

symproc <- procSym(boneLM, pairedLM=pairedLM)
symcomp <- symproc$Sym
symproc$Sym[,,1]

             [,1]         [,2]         [,3]
 [1,]  0.34726918  0.003217396 -0.016493259
 [2,]  0.39143154  0.001908742 -0.005116181
 [3,]  0.35584408  0.042833306  0.039658115
 [4,]  0.35613939 -0.049164282  0.027929753
 [5,] -0.27767625  0.069233709  0.027278709
 [6,] -0.27721126 -0.075616014  0.008812477
 [7,] -0.24989503  0.115440171  0.052299968
 [8,] -0.24911854 -0.126445769  0.021463038
 [9,] -0.35325588  0.001177840 -0.018133798
[10,] -0.04352722  0.017414901 -0.137698822

This time, symproc$Sym[3,,1] and symproc$Sym[4,,1] no longer differ just by sign of one of x, y, and z values. I would like to ask what on earth is being extracted from symproc$Sym (symmetric component after GPA in Morpho) and how does it differ from gpa$symm.shape (symmetric component after GPA in geomorph)?

Thank you!
YW

messages.body_plain:
The sign flip would only hold if the axis of symmetry coincides with primary axis of image.
Perhaps when procSym is superimposing the samples, the arbitrary rotations results in a different coordinate system that doesn't coincide with axis of symmetry. That's really a Morpho question.

messages.subject_clean: PGLS residuals violate Brownian assumption & 3D figures
messages.body_plain:
Hi geomorph community,

I have 2 inquiries: one regarding 3D figures, and one regarding residuals violating the Brownian motion assumption of a PGLS.

To give a little background, I'm studying brain shape evolution using 3D GM of N=18 mustelid species (relatively small sample size).

First, the easier question. I would love to be able to include a 3D phylomorphospace or 3D plotRefToTarget figure that essentially replicates what I'm able to do in the rgl window -- to rotate, manipulate, zoom, etc. I am aware of options such as taking a screenshot and combining multiple screenshots to create a movie, but frankly, it just does not have the same effect or relay the information in the same way. Do any of you have any experience with saving the rgl output in a way where the 3D capabilities are preserved? I've approached a couple of people with this and had no luck (I'm beginning to sense this type of code doesn't exist yet), but I thought it'd be worth it to ask all of you.

Second, I'm hoping you might have some further insights on a different issue. I'm using procD.pgls to see what ecological or behavioral variables are predictors of brain shape in this family. I used physignal to check if my PGLS residuals meet the Brownian motion assumption, which they very much do not. Whether it is "regular" residuals or pgls residuals, the K statistic hovers around 0.5 for all variables (ecological, behavioral, body size) with p-values of 0.001 or less. In addition, I ran geiger's dtt function to see if the shape data overall follow BM and MDI = -0.000495, but the plot (attached) seems to tell an odd story (which I understand may be due to small sample size). I'm concerned that I may miss out on important and significant results if the BM model is "overcorrecting" for phylogenetic relationships.

I have access to code that can help me transform the tree and force the residuals to meet the BM assumption. However, I understand that in other packages (i.e. caper), the pgls function will automatically check whether the residuals meet this assumption and transform the tree as needed. Based on a quick Google Scholar search, I am also under the impression that these sorts of transformations aren't standard practice in GM. Does geomorph have such a function available, and if not, is there a particular reason not to include it? Or is there an option to run a PGLS using a different evolutionary model (e.g. OU)? Are there other ways to analyze my data to still get at the same question?

I would greatly appreciate your insights.

Thank you,
Ani

Ani Hristova
Master's candidate
Dept. of Integrative Biology
Michigan State University

Ani,

Your mesh question was addressed by Jasmine’s response. As for the 3D phylomorphospace, if you first orient it to the position you like, the RGL has a function called ‘rgl.snapshot’ which can be used in conjunction with geomorph for generating an image (e.g., a PNG file).

As to the residuals, If they are not iid post PGLS, then one option is to use branch length transformations to attain a better fit. Caper does this using the lambda transformation. However, they are also working on univariate data; this process is less straightforward for multivariate data, and not defined for high-dimensional data (where p>>N).  In short, for high-dimensional multivariate data, these sorts of challenges have not been thoroughly investigated from a theory perspective.

However, since lambda ranges from 0 à 1, a simple heuristic approach is for you to try a few values in that range, and then use various post-hoc tests to determine whether any of these improve the issue.

Dean

messages.subject: pairwise function and RRPP procedure
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I need to use the pairwise function and I think there is a problem with test.type="dist" argument. I have a very big dataset with samples categorized in two main subdivision: males/females (M and F) and continental/island (C and I). I ran the following commands:

# isl=C/I and sex=M/F

lm<-procD.lm(coords~isl*sex, data=gdf)
gp<-interaction(dataset$isl,dataset$sex)
PW <- pairwise(lm, groups = gp)
summary(PW, test.type = "dist", confidence = 0.95, stat.table = TRUE)
summary(PW, test.type = "var", confidence = 0.95, stat.table = TRUE)

The output of the first summary gave no one pairwise statistical significance, but I know from other multivariate tests and from the biology of the species (it's very dimorphic) that it's at least all females-males comparisons should be significant. Conversely, the second summary ("var") give reasonable results, comparable with the outputs of "morphol.disparity" function. Exactly the same situation when size is considered as dependent variable.

I tried some solutions and I found that removing the RRPP procedure (RRPP=F) the outputs were much more comparable with other multivariate tests and consistent with the others analysis (big differeces between sexes and few between islands and continental specimens).

How it's possible? There is a way to fix this problem? The statistical framework it's still correct despite the correction (RRPP=F) I made?

Thank you very much.

Vasco Avramo

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] pairwise function and RRPP procedure
messages.body_plain:
Vasco,

Please review your choice of null model (see the help page).  While all male-female vectors might be significantly greater than 0, you tested whether the length of these vectors vary among each other; i.e., your implicit null model had isl and sex as factors, meaning general sexual dimorphism was held constant in the permutation procedure.  (It appears that you might have significant sexual dimorphism, but sexual dimorphism does not vary among levels of isl.)

When you changed RRPP to FALSE, you changed the null model to have just an overall mean.  It is not a problem or something that needs to be fixed.  You just need to be cognizant of the null model you are using.

Best,
Mike

messages.body_plain:
Vasco, and everyone,

I encourage everyone to learn to restate the null hypotheses, conditioned on null models.  For example, this simple null hypothesis,

H0: var(means) = 0

is correct, but imprecise.  A more precise way to say to say it is

H0: var(means) | model_i = 0.

This latter way defines the null model used to generate the sampling distributions of the statistic used to evaluate var(means).  The var(means) value will change with different null models.  Is changing RRPP = F correct?  I don’t know.  This means you are testing Ho: var(means) | intercept = 0, which is different than Ho: var(means) | isl + sex = 0.  Is it correct to do that?  It depends on your research question.

There is no simple yes/no way to answer your question, as there is no single way to test the variance among means for factorial models.

Cheers!
Mike

> > > The output of the first summary gave no one pairwise statistical significance, but I know from other multivariate tests and from the biology of the species (it's very dimorphic) that it's at least all females-males comparisons should be significant. Conversely, the second summary ("var") give reasonable results, comparable with the outputs of "morphol.disparity" function. Exactly the same situation when size is considered as dependent variable.
> > >
> > > I tried some solutions and I found that removing the RRPP procedure (RRPP=F) the outputs were much more comparable with other multivariate tests and consistent with the others analysis (big differeces between sexes and few between islands and continental specimens).
> > >
> > > How it's possible? There is a way to fix this problem? The statistical framework it's still correct despite the correction (RRPP=F) I made?
> > >
> > > Thank you very much.
> > >
> > > Vasco Avramo
